title: HubSpot Calling vs Aircall for Sales Teams — Jon Martin
seoTitle: HubSpot Calling vs Aircall: Minutes, Plans, and CTI
description: HubSpot's built-in calling versus Aircall for HubSpot sales teams: included minutes, seats, prices, and what logs to the record. Checked Nov 23, 2026.
h1: HubSpot calling vs Aircall for sales teams
dek: HubSpot already includes calling. The question is whether the minutes you pay for cover your team, or whether you need a phone system that sits on top of the CRM.
This page lines up HubSpot's built-in dialer against Aircall so you can decide on capacity first and features second.

Best for.hubspot: Teams whose monthly talk time fits the included minutes and who want to dial from inside the CRM without another vendor.
Best for.aircall: Teams that need a full phone system or calling that is not capped by HubSpot's account-wide minute pool.

What it is.hubspot: Built-in VoIP calling from contact records, the calling remote, and the inbox.
What it is.aircall: A cloud phone system with numbers, routing, and desktop and mobile apps, plus a native HubSpot integration.

Included calling.hubspot: {{fact:hubspot.calling_min_starter}}. Professional and Enterprise include more, shared across the account.

Who can place a call.aircall: Each caller needs a license, with {{fact:aircall.min_licenses}}.

What lands in HubSpot.hubspot: Calls are logged to the CRM record.

Starting price (US).hubspot: Included with a paid edition. Catalog list prices: {{fact:hubspot.core_seat_starter}}; {{fact:hubspot.sales_seat_pro}}; {{fact:hubspot.sales_seat_ent}}.

Phone system features.hubspot: Calling and logging inside the CRM, where {{fact:hubspot.power_dialer}}.

Trial or access.hubspot: Calling comes with the paid hub.

blocks.html: {{link:hubspot}} includes calling in Sales Hub and Service Hub. Minutes are a shared account cap, not a per-rep allotment: {{fact:hubspot.calling_min_starter}}, {{fact:hubspot.calling_min_pro}}, and {{fact:hubspot.calling_min_ent}}.

{{link:aircall}} is a separate cloud phone system with a native HubSpot integration. On its published US plans, Essentials is {{fact:aircall.essentials_price}} and Professional is {{fact:aircall.professional_price}}, with {{fact:aircall.min_licenses}} and {{fact:aircall.unlimited_us_ca}}.
Stay on HubSpot calling if your monthly talk time fits the included minutes. Add Aircall if you are hitting the cap or need a full phone system. Decide on capacity before you decide on features.

items: Estimate a rough monthly talk time. If it fits the included minutes, stay on HubSpot calling.
If you are hitting the cap, add capacity on Professional or Enterprise, or move the calling to Aircall.
If you need IVR, a power dialer, or calling that is not minute-capped, pick Aircall (Essentials or Professional).
Before you buy either, decide which HubSpot objects get call activity and who owns the routing rules.

blocks.html: This is a capacity and feature decision, not a moral one. There is no prize for ripping out calling you already pay for. For a broader list of options, see my roundup of calling apps for HubSpot.
